markers.title: Fourth filter chip sits off-screen
markers.body: "0 awaiting inspection" is already clipped at the viewport edge, and "0 has notes" after it sits entirely off-canvas (x≈480 in a 390pt-wide viewport). There's no fade or scroll indicator hinting the filter row scrolls horizontally, so the last chip is effectively undiscoverable.

markers.title: Header action icons under 44dp
markers.body: The filter, calendar, and settings icons next to the date each render at roughly 28-30dp square — below the iOS HIG 44×44dp minimum — and sit close together, increasing mis-tap risk.

markers.title: Room-name column width depends on status text length
markers.body: The name/type block is 171dp wide next to a "Needs deep clean" pill but 204dp wide next to the shorter "Needs clean" pill — the column isn't a fixed width, it's whatever's left over after the pill. A longer room name paired with the longer status text risks wrapping or truncating unpredictably.

markers.title: Unlabeled flask icon in header
markers.body: The flask/lab icon next to the screen title has no visible label and no obvious effect. If it's a dev-only affordance it should be hidden in this context; if it's a real feature, add a label so its purpose is discoverable.

working_well: Room rows keep a consistent 82px vertical rhythm from top to bottom, making the list easy to scan.
Status pills share a consistent right edge regardless of label length, giving the list a clean visual column.
Room name and room-type label are clearly stacked with a strong hierarchy (bold name, muted caption type).
worth_considering: Consider a sticky/collapsible summary bar so the dirty/deep-clean counts stay visible while scrolling the long room list.
Grouping rows by room type (Family Room, Bridge Room, Deluxe Suite) with section headers could reduce scanning effort versus a single flat list.
"Needs deep clean" and "Needs clean" pills use the same red/pink palette differentiated mainly by label text — an icon or shade difference would help scanning at a glance.
